title: Read the site language from site.lang
description:
This PR makes `site.lang` the key for the site's language, the name Quarto uses. great-docs read it from a top-level `language:`, while the documentation still taught `site.language`, and Quarto's own `language` key means something else (string overrides).

`site.language` keeps working; a top-level `language:` is no longer read, and `great-docs lint` now warns about both.

title: Remove the unreachable User Guide navigation label
description: This PR removes the post-render code that filled an empty narrow-screen navigation title with a "User Guide" label. Quarto now fills that title itself, with breadcrumbs or the page title, so the label could only appear on a sidebar page that has no title.

title: Use CSS for the end rule on an API Page
description: This PR moves the thin rule at the end of an objects API pages into the theme stylesheet and instead of adding a tag in the post-render.

title: Drop dead reference index rewrites from post-render
description: This PR removes two rewrites of the API reference index page from the post-render step. One converted two-column tables into definition lists and the other removed an "API Reference" entry from the table of contents. Neither can fire on current output: the index already renders its sections as definition lists, and the page title no longer appears as a heading.

title: Label reference pages in the narrow-screen navigation bar without rewriting HTML
description:
This PR movesrewriting Quarto's HTML to label reference pages in the navigation bar shown on narrow screens from the post-render.

Instead of rewriting, a similar visual effect is achieved by styling with css.

title: Write translations and text direction during rendering
description: This PR has non-English pages get their translation bundle, and right-to-left sites their text direction, when Quarto renders them. Until now a post-render step rewrote every finished HTML file: it inserted the gd-i18n meta tag and added dir="rtl" to <html> with a regex. It also emitted a gd-rtl meta tag that nothing reads, which is now gone.

title: feat: add a wide layout toggle for desktop screens
description: This PR implements a wide layout toggle option for desktop screens. When the viewport is 1600 px and up, a new floating button (above the back-to-top buttons) lets readers widen the content column (up to 1.5×) and both sidebars (up to 1.2×). Both sidebars stay visible. Once the layout reaches its maximum, it stays centered rather than stretching across ultrawide displays. The default layout doesn't change: on every page with a sidebar, the default grid is pixel-identical to Quarto's original template. The columns animate to their new widths, and the page keeps the reader's place while text reflows. Readers who prefer reduced motion get an instant switch. The choice is saved in `localStorage` and applied before the first paint, so pages don't flash the narrow layout. The button only appears on pages with a navigation sidebar (User Guide, API reference, custom sections). Below the viewport threshold every page uses the default layout. The `w` keyboard shortcut toggles it and is listed in the help overlay. Labels are translated into all supported languages. Here's the configuration (`wide_layout`, enabled by default): ```yaml wide_layout: enabled: true default: normal # or "wide" content_scale: 1.5 sidebar_scale: 1.2 min_viewport: 1600 prose_max_width: null # e.g. "110ch" to cap prose line length in wide mode ``` The floating-sidebar grid templates in `great-docs.scss` now compute their track sizes from one registered `` property, `--gd-wide-t`, which goes from 0 (default) to 1 (wide). One transition animates the whole grid. Before widening: After widening: Fixes: #362

title: Translate API reference headings and labels during rendering
description: This PR has the API reference write its headings and labels in the site language when it renders the page. Until now a post-render step swapped English text out of the finished HTML. It missed some labels: the Source link was never translated, and translated Note callouts were only caught when Quarto left them in English.

title: Generate social cards during the build instead of after render
description: This PR moves the Open Graph and Twitter card tags out of the post-render script. Post-render added them by reading each page's title and description back out of the rendered HTML, and only when SEO was enabled, though the user guide says the two features are independent. Sites with `seo.enabled: false` therefore had no social cards.

title: Require great_tables 1.1 for the docs extra
description:
This PR removes the cap that held `great_tables` below 0.22 in the docs extra.

Version 0.22 added a dependency on `multimark`, which had no WebAssembly wheel (required by marimo notebooks to be exported and run in the browser under Pyodide). `multimark` 0.4.0 now publishes a WebAssembly wheel.

title: Write page descriptions before rendering
description:
This PR moves the `<meta name="description">` tag out of post-render, where it was taken from the first long-enough paragraph of the rendered HTML. On API pages that paragraph was usually too short, so every reference page showed the site's default description in search results instead of its docstring summary.

Homepages that open with a hero or badges got the default in the same way. Nothing told the author that a page had fallen back to the default, so `great-docs lint --check descriptions` now reports those pages.

title: fix: rewrite a page's metadata only when it changes
description:
This PR stops the pre-render metadata pass from rewriting pages that already carry their head tags.

The pass checked for existing JSON-LD by searching the page source for the tag it had written. With py-yaml12 0.1.0, the version in `uv.lock`, the tag is stored as a double-quoted YAML string with escaped quotes, so the search misses it. Every build then rewrote the homepage and reference pages, and `test_json_ld_written_once` fails locally. CI passed because `pip install -e ".[dev]"` ignores the lock and installs py-yaml12 0.2.0, which stores the tag unescaped in a folded block.

title: refactor: write JSON-LD structured data before rendering
description:
This PR moves the JSON-LD structured data out of the post-render script. Post-render opened every rendered HTML page and spliced the script in before `</head>`, so the data lived in a separate step from the rest of the page metadata, which great-docs already writes before Quarto renders. Pages now get the script through their head tags like the description and social card tags. The values and the pages that carry them are unchanged.

The script is now also escaped, so a package description containing `</script>` can no longer end it early.

title: feat: write page scale-to-fit tags before rendering
description:
This PR moves the per-page scale-to-fit tag out of the post-render script and into each page's front matter before Quarto renders it. Post-render found the tag's selectors by mapping each rendered HTML file back to a `.qmd` source and re-reading its front matter. Pages written in `.md` therefore never got their overrides, and `scale-to-fit` or `scale-to-fit-min-scale` set in a directory `_metadata.yml` was ignored.

Both keys now work in `.md` pages and in `_metadata.yml`, merged the way Quarto merges metadata. Directory selector lists add up from the outermost directory inwards, the nearest directory's minimum scale wins, and a key in the page's own front matter replaces the directory value.

Versioned sites previewed with `great-docs build --watch` also get their page metadata again. Watch mode skips the per-version pipeline, so those pages were missing their scale-to-fit tags, search descriptions and social card options.

title: refactor: mark the Skills page noindex before rendering
description:
This PR moves the robots `noindex` tag for the generated Skills page out of the post-render step and into the page's front matter, so Quarto writes it into the head with the other metadata. Post-render had to scan every rendered page for a `skills.html` path to find the one page that needed the tag.

Matching on the path also caught user pages: a `skills.qmd` in any subdirectory was marked noindex and dropped from search results. Only the generated Skills page carries the tag now. Sites with `seo.enabled: false` still get no robots tag.

title: refactor: share one mechanism for tags in the page head
description:
This PR gives every feature that adds tags to a page's `<head>` one shared path into the page front matter. Before, page dates owned the only list of head tags and wrote it as inline raw HTML, so a second feature writing the same key would have produced a duplicate front matter key and stopped the render. Backticks in values also had to be turned into character references to keep the raw HTML spans intact.

The bundled metadata partial now emits these tags on every build, not only when SEO, translations, social cards or page dates are on. Pages without tags render the same head as before. Page date tags now appear ahead of the translation and Open Graph tags.

title: Add page dates and authors during the build instead of after render
description:
This PR moves the page dates and authors that show_dates adds out of the post-render script. 

Post-render also guessed each rendered page's source file from its path, so it looked for the user guide only in the project root and found no source for sections, blog posts or custom pages. A site with `docs/user_guide`, or with any of those pages, showed no dates on them.

title: fix: modify tooltip placement and fix label updates for floating page buttons
description: Both the back-to-top and wide layout toggle buttons now show their enhanced tooltips to the left (avoiding overlap with each other) and use `data-tippy-content` instead of `title` so the label updates correctly on state changes. The back-to-top button also picks up its i18n translation (translations already present in the codebase) instead of hardcoding English.

title: refactor: type-check the site generators under strict pyright
description:
This PR extends strict pyright from the renderer to the website generator, the API reference generator, the configuration module, and the interlinks, layout migration and pandoc packages. Before, parsed YAML, front matter and site configuration reached most of this code as values of unknown type, so pyright could not check how they were read. Front matter was also split from a page in several places, each with its own rules. `make type-check-strict` now checks every module that passes, and the strict set grows as each module is cleaned up.

Typing the code exposed several crashes and misreadings, which are fixed. Documenting a namespace package crashed while linking its source. A site whose `include-in-header` was a single mapping crashed when adding translated navigation prefixes. An interlinks alias written as a string, such as `aliases: np`, was split into one alias per character. Unusual but valid YAML, such as front matter that is a list, no longer stops the build.

Front matter is now read the way Quarto reads it: it must start on the first line of the page, and a `---` inside a value no longer ends the block. A new `great-docs lint --check front-matter` warns when a page gives a key that great-docs reads, such as `status`, `tags` or `last_update`, a value of a type the build ignores.

title: fix: use dark-mode colours for the row rules of tables
description:
This PR fixes the horizontal rules of Markdown tables in dark mode. On every site, the rules between rows and along the bottom of a table stayed the light-mode grey, so they showed as bright lines next to the dark vertical rules. Their colour is fixed when the theme is compiled, and no dark-mode rule replaced it. Light mode is unchanged.

Before (dark mode):

![Table with bright horizontal rules in dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07710aca-964a-449a-8025-046f76bd0617)

After (dark mode):

![Table with all rules in the dark-mode border colour](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/366bcd54-d7fc-41ec-933d-944e17db5979)

title: refactor: render member summary tables as Markdown tables
description:
This PR writes the Methods, Attributes, Classes, Functions and Type aliases summary tables on reference pages as Quarto pipe tables instead of raw HTML. Pandoc reads a raw HTML table as one raw block per tag with paragraphs in between, so anything that works from the page's document tree, such as the planned move of Markdown companion pages into a Lua filter, cannot recover it as a table.

The tables keep their layout, fonts and links. Only their rules change colour, to match the other Markdown tables on the site: in light mode the bottom rule is light grey instead of near-black, and in dark mode the top rule and row separators use the dark-mode border colour instead of light grey. The hidden header row now follows the site language, because a Markdown copy of the page shows it.

Before (dark mode):

![Methods table with light grey rules in dark mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7f2feef-a327-49c6-9dd3-55d904076f30)

After (dark mode):

![Methods table with dark-mode rules](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/134f4b03-cf90-4740-bdac-d35019d3dd9f)

title: refactor: style the reference sidebar from the stylesheet
description:
This PR drops the `gd-ref-sidebar` class that the post-render script added to every page under `reference/`, and the inline styles it wrote onto the API and CLI Index links. Reference pages already carry the `doc-reference` or `doc-api-page` body class, so the stylesheet and the sidebar and keyboard scripts now key on those. Custom CSS that targeted `gd-ref-sidebar` should do the same.

The typing-information page and the fallback pages of versioned builds had no reference class, and now have one. The MCP Index link gets the same spacing as the API and CLI Index links. On reference pages the sidebar's line-breaking pass now changes only the sidebar, where it used to rewrite every menu label on the page, the navbar included.

title: fix: keep sidebar sections open without rewriting the HTML
description:
This PR stops the post-render script from stripping Quarto's collapse markup from every sidebar. The stylesheet already keeps every section open and hides the chevrons, and the sidebar script now removes the collapse attributes from section headings on every page, not only on reference pages.

It also fixes the navbar menu button and the sidebar toggle on API reference pages narrower than 992 px, which did nothing when tapped. On those pages the script removed collapse attributes from the whole page rather than only from the sidebar.

title: fix: load site scripts on nested pages without post-processing
description:
This PR writes the paths of the scripts Great Docs ships as root-relative (`/tooltips.js`), which Quarto rewrites for each page. They used to be bare relative paths, which only load on pages at the site root, so the post-render script rewrote a hardcoded list of about 20 script tags on every deeper page. A script added without also extending that list failed to load below the root.

Every page loads the same scripts as before.

title: feat: write the latest release into the navbar configuration
description:
This PR writes the navbar's release information into the generated Quarto configuration instead of injecting it after rendering. On a site with a text title, the version badge is now part of the navbar title. On a site whose navbar shows only a logo, the version and release date reach the logo's tooltip through a header meta tag.

The badge's hover text now follows the site language, as the logo tooltip already did. Pages whose content mentioned the badge, such as the changelog, were skipped and now show it. A malformed response from the GitHub releases API no longer stops the build of a site with a changelog.

title: fix: render the GitHub navbar widget without escaping its HTML
description:
This PR builds the GitHub navbar widget so that Quarto leaves its HTML intact. Quarto escapes the text of a navbar item that has no link, so the widget arrived on every page as literal text and the post-render script restored it with a regular expression. The widget entry now links to the repository, and Quarto keeps inline HTML in the text of a linked item.

With the widget inside a navbar link, the sidebar script erased it on API reference pages, because it rewrites every navigation label there. The widget script now takes the widget out of the link before building it, which also stops a click on the widget from following the link.

title: fix: hide empty footer sections with CSS
description: This PR replaces the post-render step that deleted empty footer sections with a stylesheet rule. Quarto writes all three footer sections and fills unconfigured ones with a non-breaking space, and on narrow screens each empty one took a full row below the footer text. The footer looks the same as before.

title: fix: label the search button without patching Quarto's files
description:
This PR moves two search fixes out of the post-render script. Every site showed two tooltips on the search button, one from Quarto's wrapper and one from the button itself. On sites in languages other than English the button also read "Search", because Quarto never passes its translated label to the autocomplete library, and post-render fixed that by editing Quarto's bundled `autocomplete.umd.js` in `_site/`.

The tooltip script now does both in the browser and leaves Quarto's files as shipped. The button also gets the translated label as its accessible name. When the search box had no placeholder, screen readers announced it as an unnamed button.

title: fix: hide page actions on the homepage without rewriting its HTML
description:
This PR stops the post-render script from deleting the page-actions script from the homepage and the API and CLI reference indexes. The reference indexes already carry a body class that the script skips, so only the generated homepage needed one, and the script now skips that too.

One thing changes for site authors. With `homepage: user_guide`, the first user-guide page becomes the homepage, and post-render stripped its Copy and View-as-Markdown buttons along with the generated homepage's. That page now keeps them, like every other user-guide page.

Before:

![Blended homepage without the page buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7e902ad-a898-4a71-aee7-90edec6b7433)

After:

![Blended homepage with the Copy page and Markdown buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4123d68-22c0-45d2-bf9f-203e71006248)

title: feat: write Markdown companions while Quarto renders pages
description:
This PR writes each page's `.md` companion from the page's own document while Quarto renders it. Before, the post-render step rebuilt the Markdown by converting the finished HTML, and the conversion lost content that readers and LLM tools expected to find.

The homepage, license and skills pages had no companion at all. Great Tables output and HTML tables with lists or rules in their cells did not come out as pipe tables, Mermaid diagrams lost their source, headings shifted level, and the homepage's companion included the sidebar of site links. Companions now keep all of these. Rendering a single page with the CLI now refreshes its companion too, and 404 and draft pages no longer get one.

title: fix: render long reference sidebars once instead of on every page
description:
Quarto rebuilds a page's whole sidebar on every page that shows it. On a large API this takes much of the render time: for a large API's reference sidebar it could list about 1,500 links, and every reference page has to render it. This PR has Quarto render each long reference sidebar once and then copies it into the pages that show it.

Before rendering, each reference sidebar (`reference`, `cli-reference`, `mcp-reference`) is copied to a full `gd-full-<id>` sidebar. Only a one-page template shows that copy, and the original sidebar keeps just the links the navbar needs, so Quarto renders a short sidebar on each page. After rendering, a post-render script (`share-sidebars.py`) takes the full sidebar from the template and puts it into each page. It marks the page's link as current, opens the sections around it, restores the search crumbs Quarto takes from the sidebar, and removes the template from the site and sitemap.

Pages aren't edited: the sidebar is named through the directory's `_metadata.yml`, so freeze caches stay valid. Normal builds run this just before rendering, and versioned builds run it in each version's directory.

The output matches a plain Quarto render: every page is byte-identical, and the search index holds the same entries. On a 303-page site with a 300-link reference sidebar, `quarto render` went from 241 to 145s (about 40% faster). Larger sidebars should save more. Sites with short sidebars (such as this one, with 14, 32 and 24 links) render in about the same time as before. A full versioned build of the Great Docs site succeeded, with the full sidebar and the right current link on the API, CLI and MCP pages in every version.

title: fix: refine the CLI reference: (1) full command names, (2) sections-driven listing, and (3) localized help summary
description:
This PR makes 3 fixes to the generated CLI reference. The CLI index now lists each command by its full invocation (e.g. `great-docs init` instead of `init`), matching the command page titles. When `cli.sections` is set, it now works like `reference.sections` does for the Python API: commands it doesn't list get no page, sidebar entry or index entry, so the sidebar and the index always agree.

The Great Docs site adds `check-examples` and `ci` to its sections so they stay documented, and a new "Grouping Commands" section in the user guide explains `cli.sections`. The "Full `--help` output" label on each command page now shows `--help` as monospace and is translated to all supported languages.

title: fix: keep llms.txt generation behind one shared guard
description:
# Summary

#350 points out that every page advertises `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, but
those files are only generated for projects that have an API reference. #351
gated the places that *advertise* the files on `_llms_txt_available()`, yet the
code that decides whether the files are actually written still had three
separate, slightly different opinions about when to run. This PR removes that
drift, so a page can never advertise a file the build will not write and a file
can never appear on disk without being advertised.

Two holes are closed:

- `_generate_llms_full_txt()` only required an `api-reference` block with a
  `package`, so a project with an empty `sections` list still got a
  header-only `llms-full.txt` written while `_llms_txt_available()` reported
  `False`. This is exactly the docs-only-site case from #350, where a page
  links a file that is effectively empty.
- `_prepare_for_freeze()` called `_generate_llms_txt()` and
  `_generate_llms_full_txt()` directly, bypassing the predicate `build()` gates
  on. The freeze path could therefore leave files behind that a full `build()`
  never writes, which breaks the invariant `_prepare_for_freeze` documents:
  that the build directory ends up holding files in exactly the state a full
  `build()` would produce.

Changes:

- New `_llms_txt_quarto_config()` is the single source of truth for the
  structural half of the guard: `_quarto.yml` exists, parses to a mapping, and
  its `api-reference` block has a `package` and at least one section. It
  returns the parsed config, or `None` when the project is not eligible.
- `_llms_txt_available()` delegates to that helper and keeps the importability
  check that only it needs.
- `_generate_llms_txt()` and `_generate_llms_full_txt()` use the same helper
  instead of re-parsing `_quarto.yml` under their own, narrower conditions.
- `_prepare_for_freeze()` now wraps both generator calls in
  `if self._llms_txt_available():`, so the freeze path and a full build agree.
- Tests parametrize six `_quarto.yml` shapes (no file, no `api-reference`, no
  sections, no package, unimportable package, importable package with
  sections) and assert that `_generate_llms_full_txt()` and
  `_prepare_for_freeze()` agree with `_llms_txt_available()` in every case.
  This extends the existing `test_llms_txt_available_matches_generators` from
  the predicate alone to the generators and the freeze path.

One deliberate scope note: `_generate_llms_txt()` is *not* given an
importability check. Existing tests such as `test_generate_llms_txt_writes_file`
and `test_generate_llms_txt_b9` pin the behaviour that it writes `llms.txt` for
a package that cannot be imported, and after this change both production call
sites (`build()` Step 3 and `_prepare_for_freeze()`) are gated by the predicate
anyway, so the asymmetry is no longer reachable in a real build. I would rather
flag it here than churn those tests in the same PR; happy to follow up if you
would prefer the guard moved into the generator itself.

- Ref: #350
- Follow-up to #351

# Verification

`pytest tests/test_great_docs.py -k "llms or margin or freeze"` passes with 94
tests. The full suite was run on Windows before and after the change: 7886
passed / 112 failed before, 7898 passed / 112 failed after, which is exactly the
12 new parametrized tests and no new failures. The 112 failures are pre-existing
and environment-specific (PTY recorder, layout migration, lint, skill install,
page status, interlinks) and reproduce identically on a clean checkout.
`ruff format` reports both files already formatted and `ruff check` adds no new

title: fix: name the Python reference section `python` in `ref_section_order:`
description:
The `ref_section_order:` option now names the Python reference section `python` instead of `api`, so the name will still be unambiguous once R or Rust reference docs arrive. `api` still works as an alias, so existing configs keep working, and repeated entries are now dropped. As before, sections a package doesn't have are skipped without an error, and the `gdtest_ref_section_order` test site now covers this by listing `mcp` for a package with no MCP server.

The Great Docs site itself now orders its reference sections as: CLI, Python, MCP.

title: fix: keep every member when expanding a module in reference contents
description:
# Summary

A bare module name in `reference:` contents expands to the module's public members. If the module contained a class, expansion stopped there, and the class and everything defined after it silently vanished from the docs.

`_CLASS_SUB_MAP` was assigned inside the top-level class branch of `_categorize_referenced_objects` but read in the module branch. Names are processed in `sorted()` order, so a module that sorted before any top-level class hit an `UnboundLocalError`. The `except Exception: pass` around the member loop swallowed it and ended the loop.

```text
_categorize_referenced_objects
  for name in sorted(top_level_names)
    class   -> binds _CLASS_SUB_MAP
    module  -> reads _CLASS_SUB_MAP     # unbound if no class sorted first
               except Exception: pass   # swallows UnboundLocalError, loop ends
```

The map had three identical inline copies, pasted in across three commits. This PR deletes them and defines the map once as a class attribute next to `_sub_classify_class`. There's no binding order left to get wrong.

```diff
 GreatDocs
   _ENUM_BASES
+  _CLASS_SUB_MAP
   _sub_classify_class
   _categorize_api_objects
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, top-level class branch
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, module-member branch
+    self._CLASS_SUB_MAP.get(...)        # both branches
   _categorize_referenced_objects
-    _CLASS_SUB_MAP = {...}              # inline copy, bound only in class branch
+    self._CLASS_SUB_MAP.get(...)        # class branch and module branch
```

`_categorize_api_objects` never had the bug. Its two lookups just switch to the shared attribute, so its behavior is unchanged.

# Evidence

- **Before** (new test against `main` at [79841694](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-docs/tree/798416948ae42b9427b18a9ce1ac879c809792f4)):

  ```text
  FAILED tests/test_core.py::TestCategorizeReferencedObjects::test_module_expansion_without_top_level_class
  E   AssertionError: assert 'mymod.BDataclass' in []
  ```

  **After:**

  ```text
  tests/test_core.py: 253 passed
  ```

title: refactor: remove the post-render script
description:
This PR removes the post-render script that Quarto ran after every build. Each behaviour it once applied to the rendered HTML now happens while pages are generated or rendered, so the script no longer did anything, yet every build still copied it in, registered it, and reported a "Post-render processing" step with nothing to show.

The build log loses that empty step. It now also declares the number of steps it runs: before, it reported more steps completed than it had announced, for example "21/18 steps".

title: fix: highlight signatures during the build instead of after render
description:
This PR moves signature highlighting out of the post-render step. Post-render re-highlighted only the first code block on each page, so the method signatures on a class page kept Quarto's plain colouring, and the rewrite stopped working whenever Quarto's code-copy button was on. Quarto now highlights every signature with a grammar that gives callable names, `None` and booleans their own colours, and Pygments is no longer a runtime dependency.

Before (method signatures on a class page):

![Class page whose method signatures have plain, unhighlighted names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2acb1c3a-ad52-4538-8499-9e54f2ebcc49)

After:

![Class page whose method signatures have bold, coloured names like the class signature](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1847077f-7216-4cdd-933d-a363d5d9600e)

One-line overloads also sit closer together.

Before:

![Overloaded function with wide gaps between its signatures](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cd8aa20-8c48-41bc-8dc3-b844140e2ea0)

After:

![Overloaded function with a one-line gap between its signatures](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/562760e7-6954-4757-810e-15eb83fc9e30)

title: fix: customize the Changelog page's TOC appearance
description: The Changelog page's sidebar is now titled "Releases" instead of "On this page", translated for the site's `lang` setting, and lists only the releases without subsections (which really aren't needed here). Release entries use the monospace font of the release headings, both in the sidebar and in the mobile panel. The mobile button's tooltip and panel heading now use each page's own sidebar title, so they also follow the site language on other pages instead of always reading "On this page" in English.

title: refactor: remove the source.placement option
description:
This PR removes the `source.placement` option. The configuration guide documented it as a choice between showing the source link in the usage row (`usage`, the default) or beside the object's title (`title`). However, setting it has never had any effect. Great Docs has always placed the link in the usage row, and no version ever read the setting.

A `placement` key left in an existing `great-docs.yml` is now ignored, so sites that set it build exactly as before. The test package that existed only to exercise the option is gone too.

title: fix: stop linking to source when source.enabled is false
description:
This PR makes `source.enabled: false` remove the "Source" links from API reference pages again. Since the current renderer became the default, it linked to GitHub whenever the project had a repository URL, so sites that had turned source links off still showed them.

It also retires the last pieces of the old post-render pipeline that the renderer has made redundant. The build no longer writes `_source_links.json`, `_object_types.json` or `_constant_values.json`, and the "Generate source links" step is gone from the build log. The rules between class and module members are drawn by the stylesheet instead of being inserted into the HTML, and they now also appear between the members of a nested class. Otherwise the rendered pages are unchanged.

title: fix: hide pages until fully composed to eliminate flash of unstyled content
description:
When navigating between pages, I noticed a few FOUT-like things (the navbar would disappear and reappear, the sidebar would briefly show unstyled links without headers or icons, and the "On This Page" header would pop in last). This happened because `theme-init.js` runs from `include-in-header`, which Quarto places after `<body>`, not inside the `<head>`.

This PR fixes this with an inline `<style>` in the `metadata.html` Pandoc partial now hides the page before any body content renders. The previous approach used `visibility: hidden`, but child elements with `visibility: visible !important` (sidebar sections, TOC) could leak through, so the fix also adds `opacity: 0` on `<body>` which children cannot override. A double `requestAnimationFrame` in the reveal ensures after-body scripts (sidebar, dark-mode toggle, tags, etc.) have painted before the page becomes visible. A `<noscript>` fallback keeps pages visible when JavaScript is disabled.

Note that this fix doesn't address keeping the navbar on the screen while loading a new page. That's something that could be done in a separate PR (more involved of a fix).

title: fix: stop repeating the title in Markdown companion pages
description:
This PR stops the Markdown companion of a page from opening with its title twice. User guide pages that start their body with a `#` heading matching the front-matter `title`, such as the Great Docs introduction, produced companions with two identical level-1 headings at the top (see [`introduction.md`](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-docs/user-guide/introduction.md)).

The site's `shift-heading-level-by: -1` makes such a leading heading the page title in HTML, so the HTML shows it once. The companion filter reads the page before that shift and added the front-matter title on top of the heading. It now treats a leading `#` heading as the title, as the HTML does.

title: fix: require Quarto 1.9.18 or later
description:
This PR makes a build stop with a clear message when the installed Quarto is older than 1.9.18. The message names the required and installed versions.

The Markdown-pages extension now sets the stage at which its filter runs. Quarto's extension schema accepts that only from 1.9.18. On older versions every site fails at the render step with a YAML validation error in `_extensions/markdown-pages/_extension.yml`, and nothing in it mentions the Quarto version. The nightly gauntlet, which pins Quarto 1.8.26, fails this way for every package.

title: fix: warn instead of silently linking source to `main`
description: This PR changes how the build picks the git ref for "View source" links. When `git` could not start, for example under heavy load, the error was swallowed and every source link pointed at `main`, even on a tagged release. The build now retries once and, if `git` still cannot start, prints a warning naming the error before falling back to `main`.

title: fix(seo): emit the robots meta tag from page front matter
description: This PR makes `robots: "noindex, nofollow"` in a page's front matter emit `<meta name="robots">`, as the SEO guide already said it did. Nothing read the key, so pages the author marked noindex were still indexed. The tag appears whether or not `seo.enabled` is on.

title: fix(i18n): translate search strings where Quarto has no translation
description:
This PR translates the search box and its results for Arabic, Hindi, Romanian and Traditional Chinese sites. Quarto ships no strings for the first three and gives `zh-Hant` its Simplified Chinese ones, so readers saw "Search", "Cancel" and "No results" in English or the wrong script.

Before:

![Arabic site search showing Cancel and No results in English](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bb09382-5349-4bcd-b7c1-8d3ebc94f2e9)

After:

![Arabic site search showing Cancel and No results in Arabic](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54afb09-59e1-4eff-be62-17e4574926a2)

title: fix: load site scripts and stylesheets through plain tags
description: This PR replaces the inline loaders that inserted eleven of Great Docs' scripts and stylesheets at run time with plain `<script>` and `<link>` tags. The loaders worked out the page's depth from a `quarto:offset` meta tag because Quarto was thought not to rewrite root-relative paths, but it does, on nested pages and on sites served from a subpath. The lightbox and marimo scripts in the page head are now deferred, and rebuilding no longer adds a second colour swatch loader.

title: fix: reject unknown docstring parsers in the configuration
description: This PR makes `parser:` in `great-docs.yml` accept only `numpy`, `google` or `sphinx`. Any other value, including an empty `parser:`, stops the build with a one-line error. Before, `parser: auto` was accepted and silently turned off the RST and Sphinx docstring handling.

title: fix: copy directory metadata from the user guide and sections
description: This PR copies directory-level `_metadata.yml` files from the user guide and from sections into the build. They were left behind, so options set for a folder, such as `scale-to-fit`, never reached its pages. Blog sections already copied them.

title: fix: publish a section's directory once
description: This PR stops a site from publishing the same pages twice when a section claims the `user_guide/` or `custom/` directory that great-docs also discovers by convention. The section now wins. When `user_guide:` or `custom_pages:` names a section's directory explicitly, the build stops with an error instead of publishing duplicate URLs.

title: fix: keep the generated header whenever the Quarto config is rewritten
description: This PR keeps the generated header at the top of the build directory's `_quarto.yml`. Five build steps rewrote the file without it: page tags, status badges and three kinds of sidebar pruning. The header is how great-docs recognises the directory as its own, so a later step could stop the build with "Build directory is not a Great Docs-generated Quarto project".

title: fix: add the early theme script even when details.js is already listed
description: This PR makes the build always include the early theme script, which applies dark mode and the wide layout before the first paint. It was skipped whenever `_quarto.yml` already listed `details.js`, so those sites could flash the default theme and width before switching.

title: fix: give signature blocks a valid kind class
description: This PR fixes the kind class on signature blocks. Functions and classes in the API reference, and the usage blocks on CLI and MCP pages, carried `.doc-Kind.FUNCTION` and `.doc-Kind.CLASS`, which no CSS selector can match. They now carry `.doc-function` and `.doc-class`.

title: fix: label unannotated type variables as typevars
description:
This PR gives a type variable declared without an annotation, such as `T = TypeVar("T")`, a `typevar` badge on its reference page. The label was read only from the annotation, so the usual spelling showed `constant`, and the stylesheet had no colour or text for a `typevar` badge. `ParamSpec`, `TypeVarTuple` and the `typing.TypeVar` spellings get the badge too.

Before:

![Reference page for a TypeVar with a constant badge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18dbffee-51a6-4078-849f-3f0c0cfaa62a)

After:

![Reference page for a TypeVar with a purple typevar badge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5cfca596-7037-40a4-8701-34a07fc424cb)

title: refactor: remove unused code from the build and its tests
description:
This PR removes code that nothing reaches. `APIReference.build()` took a `page_filter` pattern inherited from quartodoc's `build --filter`, but no caller passed one, and even when set it skipped only the pages while still writing the index, inventory and sidebar in full. A second user guide copier had no caller left after the build moved to the one it uses now.

It also deletes two rendered-site tests that read `markdown_pages` from `_gd_options.json`, a key the build stopped writing when Markdown companions became a Lua filter. Both failed whenever their fixture site was built.

title: Strip rich-click markup from structured CLI help
description:
## Summary

Rich-click commands can use `[b]...[/]` / `[cyan]...[/]` markup in help text. Great Docs copied `param.help`, `cmd.help`, and the derived short help into the generated CLI reference verbatim, so those tags appeared literally in the Options table even though the full `--help` block rendered correctly.

This change strips rich markup from the **structured** fields only, and only when:

- the command is a `rich_click.RichCommand`, and
- its effective formatter config uses `text_markup == "rich"`.

Plain Click, Typer, and rich-click's `ansi` / `markdown` modes are left untouched, so literal square brackets are preserved. The full `--help` text is already rendered by Click and is unchanged.

Fixes #429.

## Tests

Added `tests/test_cli_help_markup.py` with five cases:

- rich-click option help is plain text
- rich-click command help / short help / description are plain text
- rich-click `ansi` mode keeps literal brackets
- rich-click `markdown` mode keeps its text
- plain Click help keeps literal brackets

Results:

- `pytest tests/test_cli_help_markup.py -q` → 5 passed
- `pytest tests/test_cli_help_markup.py tests/test_typer_cli.py tests/test_great_docs.py -k "click or cli" -q` → 154 passed, 1 skipped

`rich-click` is added to the `dev` extra so the integration tests run in CI.

## Checklist

- [x] I understand and agree to the Code of Conduct.
- [x] I have followed PEP 8 as best as possible.
- [x] I have added pytest unit tests for the new behavior.

title: Test CLI help uses the command's context class
description:
## Summary

Adds a regression test for `_get_click_help_text()` building the help context from `cmd.context_class` rather than a plain `click.Context`.

This is the behavior that makes help rendering work for commands whose context builds a custom formatter — Typer's vendored Click and rich-click's `RichContext`, for example. The existing `context_class` implementation is correct; this test pins it.

The test defines a `click.Command` with a custom context/formatter that requires a `config` attribute, then asserts `_get_click_help_text()` returns the usage text. Against the old `click.Context(cmd, ...)` construction the test fails with:

```
AttributeError: 'HelpFormatter' object has no attribute 'config'
```

With `cmd.context_class(...)` it passes.

## Tests

- `PYTHONPATH=$PWD pytest tests/test_cli_help_context.py -q` → 1 passed
- Verified RED by temporarily restoring `click.Context(cmd, ...)`; the test failed with the expected `AttributeError`.

No production code changes.

## Checklist

- [x] I understand and agree to the Code of Conduct.
- [x] I have followed PEP 8 as best as possible.
- [x] I have added pytest unit tests for the behavior.

title: fix: various Termshow fixes (e.g., named themes, `termshow play`, shortcode fixes, etc.)
description:
This PR makes several Termshow features that were documented but missing actually work. It adds a registry of 16 named terminal themes (dracula, nord, tokyo-night, catppuccin, solarized, and more) with inline color overrides, and implements the `great-docs termshow play` command for quick in-terminal review.

The shortcode's `poster`, `controls`, and `theme` options now take effect, an attribute-escaping bug is fixed, and rendered output is keyed by project-relative path so same-named recordings in different folders no longer overwrite each other (the build now warns when output is missing).

The editor no longer drops theme, line-height, or cursor settings on save, and the User Guide's settings reference has been corrected to match the code.

title: feat: add `termshow validate` for recordings and scripts
description:
This PR adds `great-docs termshow validate`, which checks a `.termshow` recording and its companion `.termshow.yml` script and reports each problem with its file and entry (e.g., `annotations[2].position`). Errors cover anything the format doesn't allow (malformed recording lines, unknown keys, wrong types or values, cuts that end before they start, invalid regexes), with rules taken from the published JSON Schemas at run time so no new dependency is needed.

Warnings catch valid-but-likely-wrong scripts: items timed past the end of the playback, overlapping cuts, snippets, or same-position annotations, out-of-order chapters, highlights outside the terminal, and `match` patterns that never appear on screen while active. The command accepts several files, exits 1 on errors (or on warnings with `--strict`), and is documented in a new "Validating a Recording" section of the Terminal Recordings guide.

title: feat: add animated SVG export for Termshow recordings
description: This PR adds `great-docs termshow export`, which turns a recording into a single self-contained animated SVG that plays with CSS alone, so it works as an `` in GitHub and GitLab READMEs. The export applies the companion script's cuts and speed changes, bakes in annotations and chapter labels (with optional title cards), stores each unique row and screen once to keep files small, and for light/dark theme pairs writes both versions along with a ready-to-paste `` snippet, warning when a file passes 2 MB. As for documentation, the Terminal Recordings guide gains an "Exporting an Animated SVG" section, and new tests cover the SVG structure, timing, annotations, chapters, theme pairs, and the CLI.

title: feat: add light/dark theme pairs and cursor colors for Termshow
description:
This PR adds light/dark theme pairs to termshow recordings: `theme: auto` uses the built-in `github-light`/`github-dark` pair, and `theme: {light, dark}` lets authors choose their own pair, with each side a theme name or an inline mapping. The manifest stays at version 2 and gains an optional `dark` member that holds the dark theme's colors and rows in parallel to `lines`, so a pair adds a second set of colors rather than a second set of frames (SVG files and posters use the light side). 

The player draws the side that matches the page's color mode (`data-bs-theme`, the Quarto classes, or `prefers-color-scheme`) and redraws when the mode changes. Themes also gain an optional `cursor` color, and the player's light-mode CSS, whose `body[data-bs-theme]` selectors never matched on Great Docs sites, now works through a class the player sets itself.

The schemas, the Terminal Recordings guide (with a live `theme: auto` demo), the format spec, and the tests (including node parity tests for dark-side drawing and mode detection) are now updated to match.

title: fix: draw match highlights, and keep every field when the editor saves
description:
This PR closes three gaps found while writing the termshow format spec. The player now draws `match` highlight targets: it matches the pattern row by row against the v2 cell grid, uses `group` to cover just the captured text, and with `track_scroll` follows the text as it scrolls (hiding when it's gone); without `track_scroll` the highlight stays where its text first appears.

The editor's save no longer drops `speed_map`, `badge_icon`, `fade_in` or `fade_out`. It quotes strings safely and keeps times to the millisecond, and its preview now reads the script the same way a build does. A new test saves every docs and GDG script through the editor and checks it reloads unchanged and still passes the schema.

title: docs: publish Termshow file format spec and JSON Schemas
description:
This PR adds a Termshow File Formats page to the user guide that specifies the `.termshow` recording format, the `.termshow.yml` script format, and the version 2 player manifest, including the serialization rules other tools can rely on and the versioning policy. It also adds a JSON Schema for each format under `great_docs/_term_player/schemas/`, shipped with the package and published at stable URLs on `main`, so editors can autocomplete and validate scripts.

New tests in `tests/test_term_schemas.py` check the docs and test-package recordings, the user guide's YAML examples, importer output, and rendered manifests against the schemas, and keep the schema enums in sync with the themes and player CSS.

title: enh: use compact Termshow frames with client-side SVG rendering
description:
This PR cuts the size of embedded terminal recordings by storing each unique terminal row and each unique screen once in a version 2 `manifest.json`. Keyframes now refer to screens by number, and the player draws them as SVG in the browser. Across the docs recordings, the data inlined into pages drops from ~1250 KB to 92 KB (93% smaller). The player's renderer produces exactly the same SVG as the Python renderer, which a new Node test checks, so highlights, snippets and poster images are unchanged.

The PR also fixes an older bug where float error in accumulated event times left an event out of its own keyframe, so frames showed the screen from one keystroke or output line too early, and it fixes the `gdtest_termshow` GDG site, whose recordings weren't being found and whose TUI demo had misaligned borders.

Finally, `termshow render` and the build log now report the page payload size, and the unused `deltas` placeholder is removed from the manifest.

title: feat: add asciicast export to `termshow export`
description:
This PR adds `great-docs termshow export --cast`, which writes a recording as an asciicast file (v3 by default, v2 with `--v2`) for asciinema's player and CLI and for asciinema.org. The script's cuts and speed changes are applied, its chapters become markers, and its theme (the light side of a pair) goes in the header.

Annotations, highlights, snippets and the prompt replacement are left out, and the command lists any the script has. It also fixes the parser so it reads the top-level `theme` in v2 files, which means v2 imports keep their colors.

title: feat: reproducible scripted recordings in CI, with `termshow check --json` and a workflow recipe
description:
This PR makes the shell that runs a script's steps start with a clean environment: it passes through only a few variables, such as `PATH`, `HOME` and `LANG`, so editor and CI settings like VS Code's `PYTHONSTARTUP` or `NO_COLOR` no longer leak into recordings. This changes behaviour for existing scripts, and the new `record.inherit_env: true` setting restores it.

`great-docs termshow check --json` prints the results as one JSON object, with a summary and each script's status, diffs and errors, and keeps the same exit status. The user guide gains a "Keeping demos up to date in CI" section with a GitHub Actions workflow that checks demos on pull requests and opens a pull request with re-recorded demos on a schedule.

title: feat: convert VHS tapes to Termshow scripts with `termshow import-tape`
description:
This PR adds `great-docs termshow import-tape demo.tape [OUTPUT]`, which converts a VHS tape into a `.termshow.yml` script with `record:` and `steps:`, so VHS users can move their demos over in one command. Typing, key presses (with counts and speeds), Ctrl/Alt letter combinations, sleeps, waits (including `+Screen` and `@timeout`), `Hide`/`Show`, and `Copy`/`Paste` become steps. A `Type` + `Enter` + `Wait` in a row becomes a single `run`. `Env` and the shell, typing-speed, and wait settings go in `record`, and themes (built-in names or a JSON color set), the window bar, line height, font, and playback speed go in `settings`.

The script keeps VHS's `> ` prompt, and shells start without their startup files, so a tape's waits behave as they do in VHS. Commands with no equivalent (`Output`, `Screenshot`, `Source`, `Require`, pixel sizes, and settings that only change how VHS draws the video) are listed with line numbers in the output and in a comment at the top of the script, `--record` records the result straight away, and the user guide gets a side-by-side example that a test keeps in sync with the converter.

title: refactor: make main pass ruff and strict pyright
description:
This PR brings `main` to a state where `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `make type-check-strict` all pass, so that CI can enforce them. Strict pyright reported 110 errors in the module that shares long reference sidebars between pages, although that module is on the strict include list. `ruff check` reported 11 errors, and `ruff format --check` flagged 11 files.

Most changes are type-only or formatting. Two unreachable fallbacks go: the "griffe not available" branch of docstring-style detection and an unused probe in skill discovery. Every site gets a copy of the colour-swatch shortcode, whose single-letter variables are renamed, so that file differs in every build while the pages it renders do not.

title: ci: check lint, strict types and build output on pull requests
description:
This PR adds a CI job that runs `make check-format` and `make type-check-strict` on pull requests and pushes to `main`. On pull requests it also runs the build harness: it builds 40 test packages, with Quarto rendering stubbed, on the pull request and on its base commit, and fails on any difference between the build directories. Until now these checks ran only on maintainers' machines.

Pushes skip the harness, because an intended output change would fail a comparison with the previous commit. `uv.lock` is not committed, so the job resolves dependencies afresh on each run, and a new ruff or pyright release can turn it red without a code change.

title: build: require py-yaml12 0.2.0
description:
This PR raises the `py-yaml12` floor from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0.

Version 0.2.0 wraps long strings at 80 columns when it writes YAML, and 0.1.0 never wrapped. Because great-docs accepted either, the `_quarto.yml` it generates depended on the installed version: fresh installs and CI folded long values such as the site footer, while older development environments kept them on one line. The YAML means the same either way, but local builds and CI no longer produced the same files. Requiring 0.2.0 puts every environment on the same writer.

title: feat: detect drift in scripted Termshow recordings
description:
This PR adds `great-docs termshow check`, which runs a script's `steps:` again and compares the result with the committed recording, so CI can catch demos whose output has gone out of date. Both recordings are replayed through the terminal emulator and the screen text is compared at every marker and at the end, at the recording's size, without comparing timing, colors or how output was chunked. When something differs it prints a unified diff for each point and exits 1. `--update` re-records the drifted recordings in place.

Text that changes on every run, such as version numbers, durations or temporary paths, can be masked with a new `check.ignore` list in the script or `--ignore REGEX` on the command line. The `check` section is covered by the JSON Schema, `termshow validate` and the editor's save, and the user guide and file-format reference document it.

title: fix: stop importing packages when griffe cannot load them
description:
This PR deletes the fallback that sorted a package's exports into reference sections when griffe could not load the package. The fallback imported the package by name or, failing that, the first importable package directory in the project root, and sorted the exports by runtime inspection. With a mistyped `module:` setting, `init`, `scan` and the MCP scan therefore imported and ran an unrelated package. Now the same warning is printed and every export goes under "Other", as already happened whenever that import failed.

The fallback also hid a bug. The commands that list a project's documented symbols (lint cross-references, `api-diff --graph`, `api-snapshot` and the historical API rebuild of versioned builds) looked the package up under its project name instead of its import name. For a project whose two names differ and that has no `reference:` configuration, they saw different sections from the rendered reference. They now use the import name, so the key order of a saved API snapshot can change for such projects.

title: refactor: stop hiding thirteen methods from coverage
description: This PR removes `# pragma: no cover` from the signature lines of thirteen `GreatDocs` methods, among them the site build, the preview, the link checker and the proofreader. On a signature line the comment hides the whole method body, so the coverage report gave the module 97.7% while leaving out about 1,950 statements. With them counted, it reports 92.8%.

title: feat: record Termshow sessions from scripted steps
description:
This PR adds scripted recordings: a `steps:` section in `.termshow.yml` (`run`, `type`, `enter`, `key`, `sleep`, `wait_for`, `marker`, `hide`/`show`) plus a `record:` section for the shell, terminal size, working directory, environment, typing speed and timeouts. `great-docs termshow record --steps demo.termshow.yml` runs the steps in a hidden pseudo-terminal and writes `demo.termshow` next to the script, timed as the commands really ran and with typing jitter that's the same on every run.

If a step fails, the command reports which step and shows the screen at the time, and writes nothing, so the previous recording is kept. The script's chapters, cuts and annotations keep working on top of each new recording; markers become chapters when there are none, and the Termshow Editor keeps `record:` and `steps:` as written when it saves. Both sections are covered by the JSON Schema and `termshow validate`, which now also checks a script that hasn't been recorded yet.

title: feat: Add a `<termshow-player>` element for any HTML page
description:
This PR adds a `<termshow-player>` element, so Termshow recordings can play on pages not built with Quarto, such as MkDocs, Sphinx, Docusaurus or plain HTML. It reuses the existing player code: its attributes match the shortcode options, `src` takes a render directory or a manifest URL, and a manifest can also be embedded inside the element. It also has a small script API modeled on `<video>` (`play()`, `pause()`, `seek()`, `currentTime`, `duration`, `paused`) and fires `ready`, `play`, `pause` and `ended` events.

A new `great-docs termshow assets DIR` command copies the player's script, stylesheet and fonts and prints the HTML to load them. The shortcode keeps working as before, and the PR also fixes an error the player threw when its script loaded in the page's `<head>`.

title: fix: keep citation markup out of page descriptions
description:
This PR removes raw citation markup from the meta, Open Graph and Twitter descriptions of pages whose opening paragraph cites a reference. Since descriptions are written before rendering, a page opening with "introduced by Knuth [@knuth1984], who argued…" carried that text, key and all, into search results and link previews, while the page body showed the resolved citation.

Citations in brackets are now left out of the description. On a site or page with a `bibliography`, an opening paragraph that cites a reference in its text (`@knuth1984 argues`) gets the default description, since the author's name is only known once the page renders. Sites without a bibliography are unchanged.

The PR also updates three rendered-site tests that went stale: the CLI sidebar checks now read the sidebar on the rendered page rather than `_quarto.yml`, which keeps only a stub since sidebars are shared across pages, and the Markdown companion count includes the homepage.

title: test: add versioned, freeze and watch cases to the characterisation harness
description:
This PR widens the characterisation harness that guards the `core.py` refactor. It ran only `great-docs init` and `build`, so a refactor could break versioned builds, `great-docs freeze` or `great-docs build --watch` without the harness noticing. The default tier grows from 34 to 40 cases: a versioned build from a generated repository with two tags, a freeze after a build, a watch-mode run with a source edit and an interrupt, a configuration at the package root without `module:`, a homepage hero blended from the user guide, and a README homepage with an empty metadata margin. Builds whose Gauntlet spec lists exports must also leave `reference/index.qmd`.

Two existing defects show up in the new cases: freeze prepares files differently from a build, and watch mode never picks up an edited source. The report lists them as known gaps, which do not fail the run, so a fix shows as the gap closing.

title: refactor: delete code in the core builder that never ran
description:
This PR removes code from the core builder that never ran in a build or never changed its output. Freeze preparation called four methods that do not exist, each inside a handler that swallowed the error, and snapshot auto-save had a branch for non-versioned builds that could not be reached. Other pieces had outlived their callers: a tag-slug helper, a reference-index front-matter updater that ran before the page existed, the copy of a renderer asset that no longer ships, a fallback for Python versions below the supported minimum, and three keys of the API categories that nothing read.

The multi-version guide also promised an API snapshot after every successful build. It now says after every successful versioned build, which is what Great Docs does.

title: refactor: correct the documented term-recording output path
description: This PR corrects the docstring of the build step that pre-renders `.termshow` recordings, and removes an import guard around the term player. The docstring said recordings render into `great-docs/termshow/`, but they go into `termshow/` under the build directory, which is not always named `great-docs`. The guard caught an `ImportError` that cannot happen: the term player imports only the standard library and a hard dependency.

title: fix: stop writing pragma comment text into generated homepages
description: This PR removes `# pragma: no cover` text that a bulk coverage change had left inside two page templates, so it ended up in generated homepages. On a homepage blended with the user guide, the hero's raw-HTML fence carried the comment, and Quarto showed the hero as an inline code span. On a README homepage with an empty metadata sidebar, the front matter opened with `---  # pragma: no cover`, and Quarto rejected the page.

title: fix: discover MCP servers in the documented package
description:
This PR fixes MCP server auto-discovery for projects that do not set `mcp.module`. Discovery guessed the package from the build directory's name. When `great-docs.yml` sits at the package root, that directory is `great-docs`, so with the `mcp` extra installed the site documented Great Docs's own MCP server: reference pages, an MCP sidebar and tab, and `.well-known/mcp.json`. With a `docs/` directory the guess was `default`, so discovery never found the project's own server.

Discovery now tries `<package>.mcp`, `<package>.mcp_server` and `<package>.server`, where `<package>` is the top-level `module` setting or, without one, the package Great Docs detects. `mcp.module` still takes precedence, and the MCP page of the user guide says where the candidates come from.

title: fix: accept a boolean changelog setting and reject other scalars
description:
This PR makes `changelog: true` and `changelog: false` work as shorthands for `changelog.enabled`, the way they already do for options such as `tags` and `mcp`. Before, any non-mapping `changelog:` value replaced the default settings, and the build stopped with the bare message `Error: 'changelog.enabled'`. That included `changelog: false`, the obvious way to turn the changelog off.

Any other scalar, such as `changelog: CHANGELOG.md`, now stops the build with a configuration error that names the file, the value and the accepted forms. The Gauntlet package that set that value now uses the mapping form.

title: Fix `speed_map` and cut timing in termshow scripts
description:
This PR rewrites how `apply_script` turns recording times into playback times. It now does this in a single pass over the original recording timeline: cut ranges are skipped, speed-map ranges are scaled, and the global speed is applied last. This fixes a bug where any event before or between speed segments was moved to time 0.

We also fix `speed_map` being applied to times after cuts were removed, when the docs describe it on the original timeline. Output printed during a cut is now kept and shown at the cut's start, so playback jumps to the screen as it was after the cut instead of losing it (this matches the editor preview).

title: test: add a harness that compares init and build output with main
description:
This PR adds a characterisation harness for `great-docs init` and `great-docs build`, run with `make harness` (34 cases) or `make harness-full` (every Gauntlet package). It builds each package twice, once with `main` in a separate worktree and once with the current checkout, and reports every difference: exit status, files written, the build log's steps and warnings, and the exceptions great-docs handles along the way.

The planned split of `core.py` moves methods that the existing tests patch by name, so those tests cannot show that a move kept the output the same. The harness drives the command line as a black box, one process per command, with a stub `quarto` that skips the render, so a 34-case run takes about 20 seconds and does not depend on where the code lives.

title: test: remove shadowed tests without changing test collection
description:
This PR deletes 129 test definitions that never ran, because a later definition in the same module or class reused the name and replaced them. Most are in `tests/test_great_docs.py`; one is a helper and four are whole classes. The tests pytest collects are unchanged.

The duplicates made the test files look as if they checked more than they did, and an edit to the earlier copy of a test had no effect.

title: fix: stop Termshow players picking up their poster after setup
description: This PR fixes players that grew to double height on the live site, with the poster frame (an empty screen and cursor) shown under the controls. The script's watcher for added players could set a player up while the page was still loading, before the browser had added the poster image, and the later setup pass then skipped the player because it was already set up. The watcher now waits until the page has loaded, and the setup pass handles the players already in the page.

title: feat: make the Termshow player accessible
description:
This PR makes the Termshow player work with a keyboard, a screen reader and reduced-motion settings. With reduced motion turned on, players don't autoplay or loop, they stop at each chapter, and overlays and the cursor no longer fade, pulse or blink. Keyboard shortcuts now work only while focus is in the player.

Screen readers get a labeled player, a spoken time and chapter for the slider, and announcements for chapter stops and the end of the recording. It also fixes colors below WCAG AA (including the unreadable white chapter bar on light themes), enlarges small click targets, adds tests and a new Accessibility section to the terminal recordings guide.

title: feat: export Termshow recordings as GIF, MP4, or WebM
description:
This PR adds `--gif`, `--mp4`, and `--webm` to `great-docs termshow export`, for places that can't show an animated SVG, like pull request comments, chat, and slides. Each change on screen is drawn as a still image, the same way as a `termshow snap` screenshot, and `ffmpeg` joins the images: a GIF gives each one its own delay, and a video plays at a fixed frame rate.

New `--fps`, `--scale`, and `--max-idle` options set the frame rate, the size, and how long a pause can last, and a light/dark theme pair writes two files.

title: ci: report harness differences as warnings unless they're regressions
description:
This PR makes the characterization harness fail only on regressions: failed checks, a command that starts exiting with a non-zero status, a command or case recorded on one side only, or differing environments. Other differences, such as changed files or new warnings, are still reported in full but no longer fail the run.

In CI they raise a warning annotation and appear in the job summary, and the report artifact is uploaded on every run. A new `--strict` flag restores the old behavior, where any difference fails, for refactors that should leave the output unchanged.

title: feat: add transcripts and WebVTT captions for terminal recordings
description:
This PR gives every terminal recording a plain-text transcript, written next to its manifest by the build and by `termshow render`. It keeps  everything the player shows (scrolled and cleared lines too), with chapters as headings, annotations as notes, and the prompt replacement applied. The shortcode adds the transcript after the player as a visually hidden region for screen readers, and the page's Markdown version shows it in place of the player's poster.

A new `great-docs termshow transcript` command print the transcript, or the annotations and chapters as WebVTT.

title: feat: add `termshow snap` for still screenshots
description: This PR adds `great-docs termshow snap`, which saves one moment of a recording as a still SVG or PNG for poster images, social cards and slides. The moment is chosen with `--at`, `--chapter` or `--end`, and the script's cuts, theme, window chrome and prompt replacement are applied as in the animated export. `--annotations` adds the ones showing at that moment, and a light/dark pair produces two files and a `<picture>` snippet. PNGs are made with `rsvg-convert` or `resvg` at a scale chosen with `--scale`.

title: enh: plan parallel renders with Quarto's measured startup time
description: With this PR, parallel builds now record Quarto's median startup time in `build-timings.json`, and the next parallel build plans its groups with it instead of assuming 2 s. The parallel rendering guide also now lists blog listing timestamps and `build-timings.json` as differences to expect between any two builds.

title: ci: rename the build comparison harness and let a pull request require no differences
description:
This PR renames the characterisation harness to the Quarto project diff (`make quarto-project-diff`) and lets each pull request choose how strictly CI applies it. "Harness" named a kind of test code rather than what the tool does: compare the Quarto projects that two commits of great-docs write.

Since #463, CI fails the comparison only on regressions, so a refactor that should leave every build unchanged was checked only by hand. `--strict` becomes `--fail-on difference`, and a pull request whose description ends with a hidden marker (see `AGENTS.md`) runs it that way in CI. Pull requests that change nothing the comparison covers now skip it.
